dedupe_keys.name: scottish ambulance service national demand and capacity review orh and working time solutions

description: This case study is the Scottish Ambulance Service's national demand and capacity programme, a review funded by the Scottish Government to match ambulance resources to current and projected demand across Scotland. The service commissioned two specialist consultancies, Operational Research in Health (ORH), which models emergency service demand and resource deployment, and Working Time Solutions, which designs rosters, to analyse the service's operational data. The programme had two main components: recruiting extra staff and resources to meet rising demand, and redesigning station rosters with staff so that start and finish times are staggered, meal breaks are protected and crews are less often pulled out of their areas. The service reports that it recruited an additional 1,388 accident and emergency staff over three years through the programme, and further government funding added posts to reduce on-call working in the North and West regions. Coverage is national. The programme page is free to read online; the underlying modelling reports and data are not available there. Caveats: results are reported by the service itself, and the detailed simulation methods, scenarios and response-time outcomes are not public on the page. Simulation uses: a real-world example of ambulance demand forecasting and location-deployment modelling used for capacity planning and investment decisions. Related records: the NHS ambulance handover discrete event simulation (model-ambulance-des-nhsx) and the AMBDES ambulance model (model-ambdes-p02686) are open models for similar questions.
